title: 2  Searching the literature with AI
text: There is too much literature on any given topic out there for anyone to read. AI can be a very useful tool to help you find information and summarize knowledge.
crumbs: 2  Searching the literature with AI

title: 3  Evaluating output
text:
Understanding before prediction (Del Giudice et al. 2024; Messeri and Crockett 2024). Something about the difference between output that seems to work and output that has been rigorously evaluated before being presented in a talk or paper.




Del Giudice, Marco et al. 2024. “The Prediction-Explanation Fallacy: A Pervasive Problem in Scientific Applications of Machine Learning.” Methodology 20 (1): 22–46.


Messeri, Lisa, and Molly J Crockett. 2024. “Artificial Intelligence and Illusions of Understanding in Scientific Research.” Nature 627 (8002): 49–58.

title: 4  How to?
text:
We can regularly post stories here, which we can put in different categories (sucess stories, failures, tips, new technical development, other things). Ideally, we can turn these posts into a newsletter sent out to CHEAC and automatically make a slide or two out of it to presnet in meetings.
We need to do some testing for this. Likely, each posts needs some share set of minimum requirements to do the above.

title: 7  AI rules & guides from publishers
text: What are the AI policies of the big chemical scocieties and publishing houses (AAAS, Springer, ACS, Elsevier, RCS, GDCh, Wiley)
crumbs: 7  AI rules & guides from publishers

title: 8  Transparency
text: How should be practice transparency of AI usage in our work, from usage in writing manuscripts, figures, codes, and educational material?
